questions.question: If Ishwar covers 721 km in a boat in 42 hours against the stream and he takes 15 hours with the stream, then find the speed of the stream.

Speed of stream = [Distance ÷ 2] × [ (1 ÷ Downstream time) − (1 ÷ Upstream time) ]

⇒ Stream speed = (721 ÷ 2) × [ (1 ÷ 15) − (1 ÷ 42) ]

⇒ Stream speed = 360.5 × [ (42 − 15) ÷ (15 × 42) ]

⇒ Stream speed = 360.5 × (27 ÷ 630) = 360.5 × (3 ÷ 70)

⇒ Stream speed = 1081.5 ÷ 70 = 15.45 km/hr

questions.question: While covering a distance of 37 km, a man noticed that after cycling for 1 hour 5 minutes, the distance covered by him was 4/3 of the remaining distance. What was his speed (in km/hr, rounded off to one decimal place)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Distance Ratio**: Covered : Remaining = 4 : 3

Total units = 7 units → 37 km ∴ 1 unit = 37/7 km

**Distance Covered** = 4 units = 4 × (37/7) = 148/7 km

**Time** = 1 hr 5 min = 13/12 hr

**Speed** = (148/7) ÷ (13/12) = 1776/91 ≈ 19.5 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 19.5 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total Distance = 37 km

Time = 1 hour 5 minutes

Relationship: Distance covered = 4/3 × Remaining distance

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2c0921a44f6557cc5c4b64f4fea73e875cdbc22b1d3ac3e2dc6f00424c4aa97a.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the remaining distance be **x** km.

⇒ Distance covered = 4/3 **x** km.

⇒ Total Distance = **x** + 4/3 **x** = 7/3 **x** = 37 km

⇒ **x** = (37 × 3) / 7 = 111/7 km

⇒ Distance covered = 4/3 × (111/7) = 148/7 km

⇒ Time = 1 + 5/60 = 1 + 1/12 = 13/12 hours

⇒ Speed = Distance ÷ Time = (148/7) ÷ (13/12)

⇒ Speed = (148 × 12) / (7 × 13) = 1776 / 91

⇒ Speed ≈ 19.516 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 19.5 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed, Distance, and Time Relation

The basic formula is **Speed = Distance ÷ Time**. Ensure all units are consistent (e.g., km and hours) before calculation.

Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by **5/18**. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by **18/5**.

Average Speed

If a journey is divided into parts, **Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time**. Do not simply average the speeds.</p

questions.question: From a taxi stand, two cabs start at a speed of 74 km/hr at an interval of 28 minutes, both cabs travelling in the same direction. A man coming in the opposite direction towards the taxi stand meets the cabs at an interval of 10 minutes. Find the speed (in km/hr) of the man.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__
The **distance** covered by the **cab** in the **remaining time** (28 − 10 = 18 min) is equal to the distance covered by the **man** in 10 minutes.

Ratio of **Time** (Cab : Man) = 18 : 10 = 9 : 5

Ratio of **Speed** (Cab : Man) = 5 : 9

Speed of **Man** = (74 ÷ 5) × 9 = 14.8 × 9 = 133.2 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 133.2 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9123432ef54cbdb43ca6ed0858e5a0458aa254360fcc6be57f5feac018af5f16.png] 
**Given:** Speed of **Cab** (S꜀) = 74 km/hr, Time Interval of Cabs (Tᵢ) = 28 min, Meeting Interval (Tₘ) = 10 min.

**Formula:** S꜀ × (Tᵢ − Tₘ) = Sₘ × Tₘ

⇒ Distance between two cabs = 74 × (28/60) km

⇒ In 10 minutes, the **Man** and the **Cab** cover this distance together (Relative Speed).

⇒ (74 + Sₘ) × (10/60) = 74 × (28/60)

⇒ (74 + Sₘ) × 10 = 74 × 28

⇒ 74 + Sₘ = (74 × 28) ÷ 10

⇒ 74 + Sₘ = 2072 ÷ 10 = 207.2

⇒ Sₘ = 207.2 − 74 = 133.2 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 133.2 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed

When two objects move towards each other, their **relative speed** is the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂).

Sound and Echo Logic

This problem follows the same logic as **bullets fired** at intervals where a person hears the sounds at different intervals due to motion.

Time-Speed Inverseness

For a constant distance, speed is **inversely proportional** to time (S ∝ 1/T).</p

questions.question: A boat takes 51 minutes to go 10.2 km upstream. The ratio of the speed of the boat in still water to that of the stream is 7 : 6. How much total time (in hours) will the boat take to go 17.7 km upstream and 66.3 km downstream?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Upstream speed (U)** = 10.2 km ÷ (51/60) h = 12 kmph.

Ratio of **Boat (B)** : **Stream (S)** = 7 : 6 ⇒ Upstream ratio (B−S) = 7−6 = 1 unit.

1 unit = 12 kmph ⇒ Downstream (B+S) = 7+6 = 13 units = 13 × 12 = 156 kmph.

Total time = (17.7 ÷ 12) + (66.3 ÷ 156) = 1.475 + 0.425 = 1.9 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.9 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/85e6eb55c49903355bbd7d0fa538b758983b10bb73f9357320e5a6ffe1a001fc.png] 

**Given:** Upstream distance = 10.2 km, Time = 51 min, Boat:Stream ratio = 7:6.

**Formula Used:** Speed = Distance ÷ Time; Upstream speed (U) = B − S; Downstream speed (D) = B + S.

⇒ **Upstream speed (U)** = 10.2 / (51/60) = (10.2 × 60) / 51 = 612 / 51 = 12 kmph.

⇒ Let **Speed of Boat** = 7x and **Speed of Stream** = 6x.

⇒ U = 7x − 6x = x ⇒ x = 12 kmph.

⇒ **Downstream speed (D)** = 7x + 6x = 13x = 13 × 12 = 156 kmph.

⇒ **Time for 17.7 km Upstream** = 17.7 / 12 = 1.475 hours.

⇒ **Time for 66.3 km Downstream** = 66.3 / 156 = 0.425 hours.

⇒ **Total Time** = 1.475 + 0.425 = 1.9 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.9 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Water

Upstream speed is the difference (B − S) while downstream speed is the sum (B + S) of boat and stream speeds.

Conversion of Time

To convert minutes to hours, divide by 60. Example: 51 minutes = 51/60 hours = 0.85 hours.

Speed of Boat and Stream

Boat speed B = (D + U)/2 and Stream speed S = (D − U)/2, where D is downstream and U is upstream speed.</p

questions.question: From a taxi stand, two cabs start at a speed of 54 km/hr at an interval of 29 minutes, both cabs travelling in the same direction. A man coming in the opposite direction towards the taxi stand meets the cabs at an interval of 12 minutes. Find the speed (in km/hr) of the man.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Distance covered by **cab** in (29 − 12) minutes = Distance covered by **man** in 12 minutes.

Ratio of **Speed of Cab** : **Speed of Man** = 12 : (29 − 12) = 12 : 17.

Given, **Speed of Cab** = 54 km/hr (12 units → 54).

1 unit → 54 ÷ 12 = 4.5. Therefore, 17 units → 17 × 4.5 = 76.5 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 76.5 km/hr.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/76ab5c362c7aaed0ed93f37a50941b6fdeea4c0486b20ffc8d5d55925f3fbc98.png] 

**Given:** **Speed of Cab** = 54 km/hr, **Time Interval of Cabs** = 29 min, **Meeting Interval** = 12 min.

**Formula:** Distance between cabs = Relative Speed × Meeting Time.

⇒ Distance between two cabs = 54 × (29 ÷ 60) km.

⇒ Let **Speed of Man** be 'v' km/hr.

⇒ Relative speed (opposite direction) = (54 + v) km/hr.

⇒ Distance = Relative Speed × Meeting Interval.

⇒ 54 × (29 ÷ 60) = (54 + v) × (12 ÷ 60).

⇒ 54 × 29 = (54 + v) × 12.

⇒ 1566 = 648 + 12v.

⇒ 12v = 1566 − 648 = 918.

⇒ v = 918 ÷ 12 = 76.5 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 76.5 km/hr.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Opposite Direction

When two objects move towards each other, their **Relative Speed** is the sum of their individual speeds: Sᵣₑₗ = S₁ + S₂.

Distance Constant Concept

The distance between two consecutive vehicles is always **Speed × Time Interval**. This distance is covered at the relative speed by an observer moving in the opposite direction.

Time Conversion

Always ensure units are consistent. To convert **minutes to hours**, divide by 60. To convert **km/hr to m/s**, multiply by 5/18.</p

questions.question: If Vishal covers 184 km in a boat in 48 hours against the stream and he takes 12 hours with the stream, then find the speed of the stream.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Downstream Speed (D)** = 184 ÷ 12 = 15.33 km/hr

**Upstream Speed (U)** = 184 ÷ 48 = 3.83 km/hr

**Speed of Stream** = (D − U) ÷ 2

**Speed of Stream** = (15.33 − 3.83) ÷ 2 = 11.5 ÷ 2 = 5.75 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 5.75 km/hr.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c49a6ff307910e803a3f6b259a6aeeca7ba652acfa6113adb3a40602b552cb41.png] 

**Given:**

Distance (S) = 184 km

Time taken against stream (tᵤ) = 48 hours

Time taken with stream (td) = 12 hours

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Speed of stream = (Downstream Speed − Upstream Speed) ÷ 2

**Calculations:**

⇒ Upstream Speed (U) = 184 ÷ 48 = 23 ÷ 6 ≈ 3.833 km/hr

⇒ Downstream Speed (D) = 184 ÷ 12 = 46 ÷ 3 ≈ 15.333 km/hr

⇒ Speed of Stream = (15.333 − 3.833) ÷ 2

⇒ Speed of Stream = 11.5 ÷ 2

⇒ Speed of Stream = 5.75 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 5.75 km/hr.**

**__Additional Information__**

Speed of Boat in Still Water

The speed of the boat in still water is calculated as the average of downstream and upstream speeds: Speed = (D + U) ÷ 2.

Relative Speed in Streams

Downstream speed = Speed of boat + Speed of stream. Upstream speed = Speed of boat − Speed of stream.

Ratio of Speeds

The ratio of speed of boat to speed of stream is given by (D + U) : (D − U).</p

questions.question: Mr. W travelled 370 km, 390 km and 720 km at speeds of 37 km/hr, 5 km/hr and 8 km/hr, respectively. Find his average speed in km/hr.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Average Speed** = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

Total Distance = 370 + 390 + 720 = 1480 km

Total Time = (370/37) + (390/5) + (720/8) = 10 + 78 + 90 = 178 hours

Average Speed = 1480 / 178 = 740 / 89 = 8 28/89 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 8 28/89 km/hr.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/623c98a0d2f5c506e8498399dd90ed81430e586e88d7687d0b975ac29f94a719.png] 

**Given:**

Distances: D₁ = 370 km, D₂ = 390 km, D₃ = 720 km

Speeds: S₁ = 37 km/hr, S₂ = 5 km/hr, S₃ = 8 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Average Speed = (D₁ + D₂ + D₃) ÷ (T₁ + T₂ + T₃)

**Calculations:**

⇒ T₁ = 370 ÷ 37 = 10 hours

⇒ T₂ = 390 ÷ 5 = 78 hours

⇒ T₃ = 720 ÷ 8 = 90 hours

⇒ Total Distance = 370 + 390 + 720 = 1480 km

⇒ Total Time = 10 + 78 + 90 = 178 hours

⇒ Average Speed = 1480 ÷ 178 = 740 ÷ 89

⇒ 740 ÷ 89 = 8 with a remainder of 28

**∴ The correct answer is 8 28/89 km/hr.**

**__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Equal Distances

If a person covers two equal distances at speeds u and v, then the Average Speed = 2uv ÷ (u + v).

General Average Speed Formula

Average Speed is defined as the total distance traveled divided by the total time taken: Vₐvg = ∑D ÷ ∑T.

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the same direction, relative speed is |u − v|. In opposite directions, it is (u + v).</p

questions.question: In a 2295 m circular race, Siddharth finishes one round in 85 seconds and Yash finishes one round in 45 seconds. How many different meeting points are there on the circumference if they are running in the opposite directions?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For two people running in **opposite directions** on a circular track, the number of meeting points is the sum of the simplified ratio of their **speeds**.

Ratio of time taken by **Siddharth** and **Yash** = 85 : 45

Ratio of speed of **Siddharth** and **Yash** = 45 : 85 = 9 : 17

Number of distinct meeting points = 9 + 17 = 26

**∴ The correct answer is 26.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of circular track = 2295 m

Time taken by **Siddharth** (T₁) = 85 s

Time taken by **Yash** (T₂) = 45 s

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c92c8fe820a9ba44f87c024ae03857c12c3d79b5cfe0f8868015e40672afdf5b.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Speed of Siddharth (S₁) = Distance ÷ T₁ = 2295 ÷ 85 = 27 m/s

⇒ Speed of Yash (S₂) = Distance ÷ T₂ = 2295 ÷ 45 = 51 m/s

⇒ Ratio of Speeds (S₁ : S₂) = 27 : 51

⇒ Simplify the ratio by dividing by 3: 27/3 : 51/3 = 9 : 17

⇒ Let the simplified ratio be a : b, where a = 9 and b = 17.

⇒ Since they move in **opposite directions**, total meeting points = a + b

⇒ Meeting points = 9 + 17 = 26

**∴ The correct answer is 26.**

**__Additional Information__**

Meeting Points in Same Direction

If two people move in the same direction with speeds in simplified ratio a : b (where a > b), the number of distinct meeting points is |a − b|.

Time of First Meeting

The time taken for the first meeting anywhere on the track is L ÷ (S₁ + S₂) for opposite directions and L ÷ |S₁ − S₂| for same direction, where L is track length.

Time of Meeting at Start Point

The time when they meet for the first time at the starting point is given by LCM of the time taken by each person to complete one full round.</p

questions.question: Babita travels a certain distance at a speed of 11 km/hr and double the earlier distance at 44 km/hr. She then returns to the starting point through the same route. If her average speed for the entire journey is 34 km/hr, then what is her speed (in km/hr) for the return journey?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Assume initial distance is 44 km (LCM of 11 and 44).

**Total Distance** = 44 (forward 1) + 88 (forward 2) + 132 (return) = 264 km.

**Total Time** = Total Distance ÷ Average Speed = 264 ÷ 34 = 132/17 hours.

**Forward Time** = (44/11) + (88/44) = 4 + 2 = 6 hours.

**Return Speed** = 132 ÷ (132/17 − 6) = 132 ÷ (30/17) = 132 × 17 ÷ 30 = 74.8 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 74.8 km/hr.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8bc5c2f7239546ef5fbaf650ec5951497997ce496ebf4c0f5da45e9387b67205.png] 

**Given:** Forward speed 1 = 11 km/hr, Forward speed 2 = 44 km/hr, Avg Speed = 34 km/hr.

**Formula Used:** Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

⇒ Let first distance be D. Second distance = 2D. Total return distance = 3D.

⇒ Total Distance = D + 2D + 3D = 6D.

**∴ The correct answer is 74.8 km/hr.**

**__Additional Information__**

questions.question: The downstream speed is 41 km/hr and the upstream speed is 20.5 km/hr. It takes a boat a total of 13 hours to go to a place and come back. What is the total distance travelled by the boat?

questions.question: A boat takes 83 minutes to go 33.2 km upstream. The ratio of the speed of the boat in still water to that of the stream is 8 : 5. How much total time (in hours) will the boat take to go 47.1 km upstream and 55.9 km downstream?

**∴ The correct answer is 2.5 hours.**

⇒ Total Time = (47.1 ÷ 24) + (55.9 ÷ 104)

⇒ Total Time = 1.9625 + 0.5375 = 2.5 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 2.5 hours.**

Speeds: **s₁** = 89 km/hr, **s₂** = 55 km/hr, **s₃** = 50 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

**Time (t)** = Distance (d) ÷ Speed (s)

**Average Speed** = (d₁ + d₂ + d₃) ÷ (t₁ + t₂ + t₃)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = 445 + 495 + 250 = 1190 km

⇒ t₁ = 445 ÷ 89 = 5 hours

⇒ Average Speed ≈ 62.6315...

**__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Equal Distances

If two equal distances are covered at speeds u and v, Average Speed = (2 × u × v) ÷ (u + v).

Relative Speed

In the same direction, speed = S₁ − S₂. In opposite directions, speed = S₁ + S₂.

Unit Conversion

questions.question: Train A running at a speed of 72 km/hr takes 24 seconds to completely cross train B running at 63 km/hr in the opposite direction. The length of train B is 1.5 times the length of train A. Train B crosses a bridge completely in 62 seconds. The length of the bridge (in m) is:

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Relative Speed** in opposite direction = 72 + 63 = 135 kmph = 135 × (5/18) = 37.5 m/s.

Total distance (LA + LB) = Speed × Time = 37.5 × 24 = 900 m.

Given LB = 1.5 LA ⇒ LA + 1.5 LA = 900 ⇒ 2.5 LA = 900 ⇒ LA = 360 m, LB = 540 m.

Speed of Train B = 63 × (5/18) = 17.5 m/s.

Bridge Length = (SpeedB × Time) − LB = (17.5 × 62) − 540 = 1085 − 540 = 545 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 545 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Step 1: Find lengths of trains.**

⇒ SpeedA = 72 × 5/18 = 20 m/s; SpeedB = 63 × 5/18 = 17.5 m/s.

⇒ Relative Speed = 20 + 17.5 = 37.5 m/s.

⇒ Sum of lengths (LA + LB) = 37.5 × 24 = 900 m.

⇒ LA + 1.5 LA = 900 ⇒ 2.5 LA = 900 ⇒ LA = 360 m.

⇒ LB = 1.5 × 360 = 540 m.

**Step 2: Find bridge length.**

⇒ Total Distance = SpeedB × Time = 17.5 × 62 = 1085 m.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concept

When two objects move in **opposite directions**, their relative speed is the **sum** of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂). In the same direction, it is the **difference** (|S₁ − S₂|).

Crossing Distance Rule

When a train crosses another train or a bridge, the **total distance** covered is always the **sum of the lengths** of the train and the object being crossed.

questions.question: T travelled 576 km, 630 km and 315 km at the speeds of 16 km/hr, 7 km/hr and 9 km/hr, respectively. Find his average speed in km/hr.

questions.question: Walking at (5)/(7) of his normal speed, Manish is 20 minutes late in reaching. The usual time taken by him to cover the distance between his home and office is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

When **distance** is constant, **Speed** is inversely proportional to **Time**.

Speed ratio (New : Normal) = 5 : 7 → Time ratio (New : Normal) = 7 : 5.

Difference in time units = 7 − 5 = 2 units.

Given 2 units = 20 minutes → 1 unit = 10 minutes.

Usual time (5 units) = 5 × 10 = 50 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 50 min.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0c40c0244fee48e0900104cf60b7a9349ba5fe61def14d046b557c61d0fab58b.png] 

**Given:** New Speed = 5/7 × Normal Speed; Delay = 20 minutes.

**Formula Used:** Distance = Speed × Time

⇒ Let Usual Speed = S and Usual Time = T.

⇒ Distance = S × T

⇒ New Speed = 5/7 S, New Time = T + 20

⇒ S × T = (5/7 S) × (T + 20)

⇒ T = 5/7 × (T + 20)

⇒ 7T = 5T + 100

⇒ 2T = 100

⇒ T = 50 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 50 min.**

**__Additional Information__**

Inverse Proportion Rule

If a person travels at a/b of their usual speed, the new time taken is b/a of the usual time.

General Formula for Late/Early

Usual Time = (Late time × a) ÷ (b − a) where new speed is a/b of usual speed.

Average Speed

For two equal distances covered at speeds x and y, Average Speed = 2xy/(x + y).</p

questions.question: Walking at 4/5 of his normal speed, Vishal is 25 minutes late in reaching his office. The usual time taken by him to cover the distance between his home and his office is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Speed ratio** is given as 4 : 5 (New : Normal).

Since **distance** is constant, the **time ratio** is the inverse of the speed ratio, i.e., 5 : 4.

Difference in time units = 5 − 4 = 1 unit.

Given, 1 unit = 25 minutes.

Usual time (4 units) = 4 × 25 = 100 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 100 min.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fb5e3384fe6a00f1a251d495ba1e99b6f188f691fa87bfbe5b1af03429f6aa78.png] 

**Given:**

New Speed = 4/5 of Normal Speed

Time delay = 25 minutes

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time | If Distance is constant, Speed₁ × Time₁ = Speed₂ × Time₂

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let usual speed be **S** and usual time be **T**.

⇒ New speed = (4/5)S and New time = T + 25

⇒ S × T = (4/5)S × (T + 25)

⇒ T = (4/5)(T + 25)

⇒ 5T = 4T + 100

⇒ T = 100 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 100 min.**

**__Additional Information__**

Inversely Proportional Relation

When **Distance** is constant, **Speed** is inversely proportional to **Time** (S ∝ 1/T). If speed becomes a/b of its original, time becomes b/a of its original.

Relative Speed

For two objects moving in the same direction, relative speed = S₁ − S₂. For opposite directions, relative speed = S₁ + S₂.

Average Speed Formula

When equal distances are covered at speeds x and y, Average Speed = 2xy ÷ (x + y).</p

questions.question: In a 2100 m circular race, Amit finishes one round in 42 seconds and Sumit finishes one round in 75 seconds. How many different meeting points are there on the circumference if they are running in the opposite directions?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **time taken** by Amit and Sumit to complete one round = 42 : 75 = 14 : 25.

Since **Speed** is inversely proportional to **Time**, Ratio of **speeds** (u : v) = 25 : 14.

For **opposite directions**, Number of **distinct meeting points** = u + v.

Number of meeting points = 25 + 14 = 39.

**∴ The correct answer is 39 points.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f727ed306389e418b547665a2b1c7d04282eb26753ce525182e638f4d99805af.png] 

**Given:** Track Length = 2100 m, TAₘᵢₜ = 42 s, TSᵤₘᵢₜ = 75 s.

**Formula:** Speed = Distance ÷ Time; Distinct points (opposite) = Ratio of speeds (a + b) where a/b is in simplest form.

⇒ Speed of Amit (SA) = 2100 ÷ 42 = 50 m/s

⇒ Speed of Sumit (SS) = 2100 ÷ 75 = 28 m/s

⇒ Ratio of Speeds SA : SS = 50 : 28

⇒ Simplest Ratio = 25 : 14

⇒ Number of distinct meeting points = 25 + 14 = 39

**∴ The correct answer is 39 points.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Meeting Points in Same Direction

If two people run in the **same direction** with speeds in the simplest ratio a : b (a > b), the number of distinct meeting points is (a − b).

Time of First Meeting

The time taken for the **first meeting anywhere** on the track is Track Length ÷ Relative Speed.

Time of Meeting at Starting Point

The time when they meet for the first time at the **starting point** is the LCM of the time taken by each to complete one full round.</p
